control_id: # HOW EACH CONTROL WAS EXECUTED
# For EACH control the SAME mutated C source tree was built TWICE:
#   selector-OFF build: the legacy C predicate is the ACTIVE authority
#   selector-ON  build: the legacy C predicate is COMPILED OUT and the
#                    compiled PolyC subject is the active authority
# THE WITNESS PROGRAMS
#   C-OFF-CA  witness-ca-compound-assign   (x += 20; the returned value)
#   C-OFF-PO  witness-po-logical-and       (p && q)
#   C-OFF-RO  witness-po-pointer-less-than  (p < q)
# A "COMPILE_FAILED" witness value means the COMPILER REJECTED the witness
# program. That IS a semantic difference of the migrated decision, because
# the rejection comes from the compiler's own type checking, which consumes
# the classifier's answer. It is NOT a build failure of the compiler itself:
# every one of these compiler builds exited 0.
# THE DORMANCY CONCLUSION, which is the point of these controls:
#   For EVERY one of the three legacy C rules:
#     - the selector-OFF build's behaviour CHANGES when the legacy C rule
#       is mutated  =>  the legacy C rule is LIVE when the selector is OFF;
#     - the selector-ON build's behaviour DOES NOT CHANGE AT ALL when the
#       same legacy C rule is mutated  =>  the legacy C rule is DORMANT in
#       the production ON build.
# The selector-ON witnesses of all three controls are IDENTICAL to the
# pristine production compiler's witnesses.
# THE PRODUCTION ON BUILD WAS REBUILT FROM THE MUTATED C SOURCE
#   C-OFF-CA_ON_CONFIGURE_RC=0
#   C-OFF-CA_ON_BUILD_RC=0
#   C-OFF-PO_ON_CONFIGURE_RC=0
#   C-OFF-PO_ON_BUILD_RC=0
#   C-OFF-RO_ON_CONFIGURE_RC=0
#   C-OFF-RO_ON_BUILD_RC=0
# (a compiler BUILD FAILURE would NOT have counted as a semantic
#  difference: NC-21)
